SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE OVERVIEW -- REVISION HISTORY (ARCHIVE)
============================================================

============================================================
1. PURPOSE
============================================================

This instance document holds the COMPLETE Section 14
revision history of 0500000 System_Architecture_Overview,
dv1_150 through dv1_0, preserved verbatim. It is the
authoritative archive of the 0500000 revision record.

It was created at TB00551 by relocating the Section 14
revision history out of the live 0500000 design document.
The live 0500000 Section 14 retains only the consolidation-
campaign-forward entries (the campaign-seed entry dv1_113 /
TB00395 Phase 0 and all later entries, plus the dv1_151
relocation entry); every earlier entry (dv1_112 -> dv1_0)
lives here. The complete record (dv1_150 -> dv1_0) is
preserved in this document.

This is a historical / forensic record, NOT a design source.
Per the binary architecture test (DEC-096) revision-history
narrative is not trading-organism architecture and does not
belong in a 0500000 design diagram; it is preserved in its
correct home here. No architectural decision, hard rule,
namespace token, parameter, or diagram content is defined in
this document; all such content remains canonical in the
0500000 diagrams (DD-001 / DD-002).

SCOPE EXTENSION (dv1_1; TB00635 / DEC-123). Beyond the Section
14 revision history, this archive is now ALSO the append-only
home for the REMAINING live-0500000 provenance relocated under
DEC-123 Phase M: (1) the campaign-era Section 14 entries
(dv1_113 / TB00395 forward) that the TB00551 relocation left in
the live diagram; (2) the figcaption OPTION-R provenance /
extension stacks; (3) the root <desc> R-increment chains
(R-increment / -prior / -prior-2 / -prior-3); (4) the V-040
design-completeness attestation blocks. Each is relocated
VERBATIM and is thereafter APPEND-ONLY here; the live 0500000
retains only live governing content + each figure's CURRENT
R-number + a pointer to this archive. Going forward, every
0500000 amendment appends its provenance entry here rather than
stacking it into the diagram (TB00000 4.6; 0311003 VP-008;
0311001 15.16.3). Binary test DEC-096: provenance is
document-control, not design content. The relocation proceeds
one figure per session (DEC-003 Path A); until a given figure's
Phase-M session lands, that figure's provenance remains in the
live diagram.

3. SOURCE AND FIDELITY
============================================================

Source: 0500000_System_Architecture_Overview Section 14, as
of 0500000 dv1_150 (the version live in GitHub HEAD when
this archive was created at TB00551).

The body in Section 4 below is the verbatim Section 14
content of 0500000 dv1_150, extracted byte-for-byte, newest
entry (dv1_150) first through oldest (dv1_0). It preserves
the source document's HTML markup exactly -- the <pre>
scaffolding tags and the HTML entity encodings (for example
&lt; &gt; &amp; &sect; &mdash; &quot;) appear here exactly as
they appear in the 0500000 source. The content is preserved
in its source form, not re-rendered, so this archive
round-trips byte-for-byte against the 0500000 Section 14
source. Pre-existing gaps in the source entry sequence (for
example absent dv1_100..dv1_110 / dv1_120 / dv1_130 / dv1_140
/ dv1_141 entries that were never authored) are preserved
as-is and are NOT reconstructed; no entry text is fabricated.

<strong>A-25 (dv1_144) ★ Keepalive, Sequence-Gap Recovery, and Connection Logging (DD-002 prose-follows-diagram for the D1 mod:WS_Manager dv1_144 migration; TB00532):</strong>
<br>
     The diagram mod:WS_Manager constraints &lt;desc&gt; is canonical for these wire facts (SD-9-verified vs 0411001 dv1_13):
<br>
     (i) Dead-connection: a sent application ping that receives no Kraken pong within 10 seconds marks the connection dead and forces reconnect [WS-PING-002, 0411001 L980-981].
<br>
     (ii) Zombie detection: WS Manager tracks last_real_data_time per connection; if time.monotonic() minus last_real_data_time exceeds 90 seconds the connection is a zombie — log ZOMBIE_CONNECTION_DETECTED and reconnect [WS-ZOM-003, 0411001 L1008-1011].
<br>
     (iii) Executions sequence gap: on a sequence jump greater than 1 on the executions stream, alert EXECUTIONS_SEQUENCE_GAP immediately and trigger a REST GetOpenOrders reconciliation [WS-EXE-019, 0411001 L576-578] — prevents Position Mirror desync.
<br>
     (iv) Balances sequence gap: on a sequence jump greater than 1 on the balances stream, alert BALANCES_SEQUENCE_GAP immediately and trigger a REST balance reconciliation [WS-BAL-005, 0411001 L607-608] — prevents capital-calculation error.
<br>
     (v) Connection logging: log connection_id on every new WS connection as WS_CONNECTED(uri, connection_id); connection_id enables Kraken support diagnosis [WS-STAT-006, 0411001 L289-292].
</p>

<strong>A-33 (dv1_152) &#9733; REST Connection, Authentication, and HTTP-Client Primitives: Headers, Nonce, aiohttp Session Config, Base URLs, and Per-Key Permission Scopes (DD-002 prose-follows-diagram for the D1 container:Kraken_REST_API dv1_152 CLUSTER R1 migration; TB00559):</strong>

     The diagram container:Kraken_REST_API constraints &lt;desc&gt; is now canonical for the eleven CLUSTER R1 REST connection / authentication / HTTP-client wire facts (SD-9-verified vs 0411002 dv1_1; the first of six clusters in the TB00558 D1 REST-API Fact-Level Gap Register). AUTH: every private REST call carries three headers — API-Key (the TRADE key value), API-Sign (the HMAC-SHA512 signature per the already-canonical WS-AUTH-002 signing model), and Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded — plus a strictly-increasing integer nonce constructed as int(time.time()*1000); Kraken rejects any call whose nonce is more than 10,000 ms behind current time, so the VPS clock must be NTP-synchronized [REST-AUTH-003 / 004 / 005]. HTTP CLIENT: all REST uses a single process-lifetime aiohttp.ClientSession (the synchronous requests library is prohibited because it blocks the asyncio loop) configured with ClientTimeout(total=10, connect=5, sock_read=8) and TCPConnector(limit=10, limit_per_host=5, force_close=False) — force_close=False keeps HTTP keepalive so the TCP connection is reused across calls [REST-HTTP-001 / 002 / 004 / 005]. ENDPOINTS: both private and public REST use base URL https://api.kraken.com, private endpoints POST to /0/private/[Endpoint], public endpoints GET or POST to /0/public/[Endpoint] [REST-HTTP-006 / 007]. KEYS: TothBot uses two API keys whose permission scopes differ — the DATA key holds query-only scopes (Query Funds, Query Open Orders and Trades, Query Closed Orders) and MUST NOT be able to trade, while the TRADE key adds Create and Modify Orders + Cancel and Close Orders; both are stored on the VPS, never hardcoded, loaded from an environment variable or encrypted config at startup [REST-KEY-003 / 004]. These eleven facts are TothBot-organism (Kraken event-source) connection architecture per the binary test and are now derivable from the D1 diagram alone (DD-014); all eleven were confirmed absent from the live dv1_151 diagram-alone corpus before encoding (RR-SCOPE-010). REST-ERR-005 is the general REST rate-limit policy and is distinct both from the WS rate-limit mechanism already canonical at ar:AR-030 / ar:AR-080 and from the GetOHLCData-specific HTTP-429 stale-regime path narrated at A-24, which the CLUSTER R2 REST-OHLC-009 entry only cross-references by label; its own WARN / back-off-5s / escalate-after-3 policy was not derivable from the diagram alone and is encoded this amendment.
